hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a TESTER (writing and running Python tests with pytest). If you are NOT in a testing role (e.g. you are an engineer, grader, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to testing sessions. If you ARE the tester, check: testers must NOT modify production source or deploy. BLOCK: rm targeting production src/ or app/ directories, docker build/push, kubectl apply/delete, helm install/upgrade, git push --force to main/master, git reset --hard, npm/yarn publish. ALLOW: pytest, pip install (for test dependencies), git push (non-force), rm in test directories, docker logs, all read commands. Respond {"ok": true} if the command is safe for a tester, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Testers must not modify production source"} if blocked.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a TESTER (writing Python test files). If you are NOT in a testing role (e.g. you are an engineer, grader, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to testing sessions. If you ARE the tester, check: testers may ONLY write test infrastructure files. ALLOW: test_*.py, conftest.py, pyproject.toml (pytest config), pytest.ini, setup.cfg. BLOCK: database migration files (migrations/, alembic/versions/), deployment configs (deploy/, infra/, terraform/, helm/, k8s/, .github/workflows/), Dockerfiles, docker-compose files, production Python source (.py files that are NOT test_*.py or conftest.py). Respond {"ok": true} if the file is allowed for a tester, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Testers may only write test files (test_*.py, conftest.py)"} if blocked.

You are a senior Python test engineer reviewing a test file that was just written or edited. Context: $ARGUMENTS.

Check for the following issues:
1. Missing async markers — any test function calling an async function or using 'await' must be decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio (or the equivalent async test marker). Flag any 'async def test_' functions that lack this marker.
2. Incorrect fixture scope — fixtures that create expensive resources (database connections, containers, HTTP clients) should use scope='session' or scope='module', not the default function scope. Flag fixtures that appear expensive but use the default scope.
3. Missing assertions — any test function that contains no assert statement (including pytest.raises, assert_called, assertAlmostEqual, etc.) is meaningless. Flag test functions with zero assertions.
4. Bare exception handling — 'except Exception: pass' or 'except: pass' silently swallow failures and must not appear in test code. Flag any bare or pass-through exception blocks.
5. Hardcoded test data — email addresses, UUIDs, passwords, API keys, or database URLs hardcoded inline in tests instead of using fixtures or factories. Flag these and suggest moving them to conftest.py fixtures.
6. Missing pytest.mark categorisation — tests that exercise network, database, cloud APIs, or slow operations should be marked with an appropriate pytest.mark (e.g., @pytest.mark.integration, @pytest.mark.slow, @pytest.mark.cloud). Flag unmarked tests that clearly belong to one of these categories.

Respond with {"ok": true} if none of these issues are present, or {"ok": false, "reason": "<concise list of specific violations found with line-level guidance on how to fix each one>"} if any issues are found.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved writing or running Python tests. If NO test files were created, modified, or executed in this session (e.g. this was a grading, engineering, or debugging session), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to testing sessions.

If tests WERE written or run, verify:
1. All test files created — every test module or category mentioned in the task has a corresponding test_*.py file. If the task asked for tests covering multiple categories (unit, integration, contract, performance, etc.), verify at least one test file per category exists.
2. Representative tests per category — each test file contains more than a trivial number of tests (more than one placeholder). Tests should cover the happy path, at least one error/edge case, and boundary conditions for the feature under test.
3. TODOs for gaps — where full test coverage was not achievable in this session (e.g., requires a live service not available in CI), a TODO comment or pytest.mark.skip with an explanatory message is present so gaps are visible rather than hidden.
4. conftest fixtures for all referenced fixtures — every fixture name used in test function arguments exists either in the same file, in a conftest.py in the same directory, or in a parent conftest.py. There should be no dangling fixture references.
5. No broken imports — all import statements reference modules that exist in the project (standard library, installed packages, or local source). There should be no ImportError-causing imports left in the written files.

Respond with {"ok": true} if all criteria are satisfied, or {"ok": false, "reason": "<specific description of which criteria failed and what must be done to satisfy them before stopping>"} if any are not met.
